text: Built S-real (ai-runs, plan-work only; all other modules land in _other as plain uncommented JS). follow.mjs: 1840 unknown-kind reads (639 src/index.mjs, 2 schema, 1 checks, 1198 in tests); entries of ai-runs used: aiRunsOf, AiRuns##accountFor, AiRuns#openMany. Each read counts once per distinct file:line+text, so a chain w.a.b counts twice.

Read all of src/index.mjs (1254 lines) once, ~15 min. Almost every unknown read in src roots in deps (untyped constructor argument) -> providers -> their answers (plan, action, filings, escalations...), the SQL rows (this.sql from deps.storage), and the destructured args of each public method.

Before comments follow.mjs says plan-work uses ai-runs entries aiRunsOf (lines 46, 1184: the import and the factory call), AiRuns##accountFor (lines 211,213,216,549,552,996: m.key, o.p.id, t.kind... nothing to do with ai-runs; a probe with plan-work alone in the program finds no symbol there, so it is a quirk of the whole program; not chased further, ~5 min) and AiRuns#openMany (lines 776, 955: run.run, place.target). The real call ai.open (line 878) is not seen, since ai is anything.

Probe: the providers' factories (actionPlansOf, actionsOf) read as returning anything even through the reader's own inference from their JS, so nothing can be @import-ed from them; every shape plan-work relies on must be written here from plan-work's own reads.
Wrote the first block of typedefs (~260 lines) for the providers' answers and the deps, from plan-work's own reads (no provider code read except action-plans' refusal helpers' first lines).

False start: in a batch edit I wrote a new statement (const marks2 = [];) instead of a comment on the existing one; caught on reading the result, removed before any build. Typing a local array by a comment means putting the comment before its own declaration, which a batch replacement got wrong.

Source at 0 unknown reads (642 -> 0) after ~400 comment lines: typedefs for 10 providers' answers, casts at each #maybe, @param on every method and helper. Typing aiRuns as Pick<AiRuns,'open'> through @import makes the tool see AiRuns#open (it did not before); with a typedef of plan-work's own it would not have. Tests: 1196 left.

Tests read plan-work's own answers (r.waits.find(...)). The reader infers each answer as a union of a refusal and the answer, ok widened to boolean on both, so a test's assert.equal(r.ok, true) cannot narrow it and every field read is an error, read as anything. So making the tests followable needs plan-work's own interface written out first: @returns {Refusal | XOk} with ok: true, per public method (what a provider's first comments would hold anyway). Then the world of action-plans' fixture (any), which every test reads ~500 times.

plan-work's own answer kinds (~180 lines: @returns {Refusal | X} on 26 public methods) plus a World typedef in its test fixture (~75 lines, from action-plans' fixture, 284 lines read) took the count from 1196 to 324. The answers' ok: true lets each test's assert.equal(r.ok, true) narrow.

matters.test and timeline.test at 0: @param {World} on each test helper, a cast to plan-work's own answer kind wherever a test reads an answer without first asserting ok (the reader cannot narrow then), and a typedef for conformance's test scene (another module's test world). 107 left.

28 left: calls by a name held in a variable (w.pw[name], planWorkOps(...)[op]: 9), the op tests' helpers, two reads of membership's MEMBERSHIP_CHECKS (any: membership states no kind), and reads through a union of answer kinds (from is null | string | object; reexamined's items).

0 unknown reads. Last 28: calls by a name in a variable cast to a ByName record (invariants) or to keyof PlanWorkOpMap (ops, declared-ops; planWorkOps given @returns {PlanWorkOpMap}), the declared-ops helpers typed, MEMBERSHIP_CHECKS cast at its two reads, two union reads cast.
